category: Decentralized CDN — paid per MB in USDC, iroh transport

free_tier.stated: No free capacity. No storage tier at all: 'Not a blockchain or storage network — durability relies on cheap, reliable object storage (S3-class) owned by origin operators.' Target delivery price $0.01/GB (node default rate `payment.rate_per_mb = 10` = $0.00001/MB).

egress.terms: $0.01/GB target, set per node and signed into every quote; client sets a ceiling. Testnet is sponsor-funded with a capped allowance — 'there is nothing to pay and no account to make' — but that is testnet money on Arbitrum Sepolia.

interface_detail: Client SDK (Rust; macOS/Linux/Windows, phone/browser in testing) + `decdn` CLI: `decdn get 'decdn:<blake3hash>/?ns=1'`. One human-verification step in a browser on first install.
tooling: Install via `curl -fsSL https://up.decdn.org/decdn.sh | sh -s -- get '<uri>'` (both scripts returned HTTP 200); PowerShell variant; node operator side is `decdn setup` / `decdn node bond`.
chaining: Origin node in front of your own S3/R2/B2/NFS/local disk stays hidden; bonded nodes cache and re-serve over iroh QUIC with bao-encoded verified streaming. Multi-source fetch splits blobs >64 MiB across up to 4 nodes, one per operator. Publisher's own origin pulls are free — cache misses cost the *serving node*, not the publisher.

limits_note: Per-MB payment is mandatory for clients on mainnet — there is no free reader tier. Namespaces gate the origin role ('Once you get approved, the rest of the network accepts your nodes as origins'), so publishing is write-gated by a human. Node bond on testnet is 50,000 TOKEN for anything up to ~1 Gbps; unbonding takes 14 days. 0.4% verification overhead plus node-to-node pull costs.
reliability_note: Public testnet only (Arbitrum Sepolia, launched 2026-10-13); governance hash blacklist forces nodes to stop serving a listed hash within 24 h, and the origin role is approval-gated.
